title: "Engineering Stories"
description: "From architecture to audio drama — turn real technical systems into short, educational audio stories, independently of any vendor."
order: 1

## Course overview

**Engineering Stories** teaches a single discipline: how to transform a real
technical system into a short, educational **audio drama** — without ever
abandoning the engineering model underneath it.

The foundational principle of this course:

> *We do not simplify technology by abandoning its engineering model. We
> understand the model first, transform it deliberately, and use story to make
> that understanding accessible.*

## Why audio drama?

Audio is one of the most constrained media to write for — *if the listener
cannot hear it, it does not exist.* That constraint forces you to be precise:
every important action must reach the ear through dialogue, narration, sound,
or music. This makes audio an excellent *test* of how well you really
understand your system and how clearly you can explain it.

## What you will learn

The course is organized as a reverse-engineering journey. You first
**experience** a finished audio story (the Crossplane restaurant), then
**deconstruct** how it was built, and finally **construct** your own.

- **Module 1 — Engineering Through Stories** — what technical storytelling is,
  its benefits and risks.
- **Module 2 — Find the Technical Truth** — model the system *first*, before any
  metaphor.
- **Module 3 — Design the Metaphor** — translate the model into a familiar world.
- **Module 4 — Cast the System** — turn responsibilities into characters.
- **Module 5 — Design the Scenes** — break the explanation into scenes.
- **Module 6 — Write the Audio Screenplay** — the audio-first intermediate
  representation.
- **Module 7 — Produce with Generative AI** — render the screenplay to audio.
- **Module 8 — Listen Like an Engineer** — review, evaluate, and iterate.

## The reference implementation

The course is built around the **Crossplane restaurant** — a canonical worked
example that maps Crossplane architecture onto a restaurant kitchen:

| Crossplane | Restaurant |
| --- | --- |
| XRD | Menu |
| XR | Order |
| Composition | Recipe |
| Managed Resources | Prepared components |
| Provider | Kitchen capability |

Read the complete worked example in the
[Reference example](reference-example/README.md). You will reverse-engineer it
throughout Part 1, then apply the process to your own concept.

## Prerequisites

No prerequisites. A basic familiarity with any declarative system (e.g.
Crossplane, Kubernetes, GitOps) helps but is not required — Module 2 shows you
how to extract the technical truth from documentation even for technology you
have not used before.

## Structure

- **Part 1 — The Craft** (Modules 1–4): the architectural principle, modeling
  truth, designing metaphor, casting characters.
- **Part 2 — The Production** (Modules 5–8): scenes, screenplay, generative
  production, and engineering-style review.
- **The Lab**: turn an engineering concept of your choice into a 2–5 minute
  educational audio drama, evaluated with the five-dimension rubric.

## Get started

Open [Part 1](part-1/index.qmd) and begin with
[Module 1](part-1/01-engineering-through-stories/index.qmd) — where you will
first *hear* the Crossplane story before you learn how it was made.
